h: Spot the Landmarks From the Top
p: Part of the fun of any big wheel is playing a game of I-spy once you're up there, and Clacton gives you plenty to pick out. Look inland and the town spreads out behind the seafront, with Pier Avenue running straight back from the pier towards the shops and the station. Along the coast to the north-east you're looking towards Holland-on-Sea, with Frinton and Walton beyond, while to the south-west the shoreline curves away towards Jaywick.

Keep an eye out for the neat rows of beach huts lining the prom, the clifftop gardens with their flower beds, and the boats bobbing about offshore. Kids love trying to spot their own car in the car park, which is far harder than it sounds.

Sit facing the sea on the way up if you can, so the big reveal hits you as you climb. Phones can get slippery with cold hands, so keep a firm grip or use a wrist strap. If anyone's a bit nervous of heights, the gentle pace of an observation wheel makes it a great first step, and sitting in the middle of the gondola rather than right by the window helps.

A ride on the wheel works brilliantly as a finale. Do the beach in the morning, chips on the prom at lunchtime, the rest of the pier's attractions in the afternoon, then finish up high as the light turns golden. Clacton has had a pier since 1871, and seeing the whole thing laid out beneath you gives you a real sense of how far it reaches out over the water. Once you're back down, the seafront gardens and a walk west along the prom make a gentle way to wind the day down.
